Source: https://arraysingenieria.com/pm-surya-ghar-subsidy/

Guide · Schemes

# PM Surya Ghar: Muft Bijli Yojana 2026: Subsidy, Eligibility and How to Apply

India's rooftop solar scheme for homes: up to Rs 78,000 central subsidy, support for housing societies, low-cost loans and the national portal. What you get, who qualifies, and the steps from application to subsidy.

On this page

- What the scheme offers
- Who can apply
- How to apply, step by step
- Getting the most from a home system
- Where Arrays Ingenieria fits
- Frequently asked questions
- Sources

By the [Arrays Ingenieria engineering team](https://arraysingenieria.com/about/) · Updated 11 Oct 2026 · 3 min read

**Key takeaways**

- Central subsidy: **Rs 30,000 for 1 kW, Rs 60,000 for 2 kW, Rs 78,000 for 3 kW or more**
- Housing societies and RWAs get **Rs 18,000 per kW** for common facilities, up to 500 kW
- Approved by the Cabinet on 29 February 2024 with an outlay of **Rs 75,021 crore**; the government's target is 75 lakh households by December 2026, on the way to 1 crore
- Modules must be Indian-made (DCR), installed by a registered vendor, and the application made on the national portal
- Many states add their own top-up subsidy; check your DISCOM

## What the scheme offers

**PM Surya Ghar: Muft Bijli Yojana** was launched by the Prime Minister on 13 February 2024 and approved by the Union Cabinet on 29 February 2024 with an outlay of **Rs 75,021 crore**. It aims to put rooftop solar on one crore homes so that each can generate up to about 300 units a month, and the government's milestone is **75 lakh households by December 2026**.

Central financial assistance under PM Surya Ghar

| Category | Support | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Homes, 1 kW | Rs 30,000 | 60% of benchmark cost for the first 2 kW |
| Homes, 2 kW | Rs 60,000 |  |
| Homes, 3 kW or more | Rs 78,000 (cap) | 40% of the additional cost between 2 and 3 kW; no extra subsidy above 3 kW |
| Housing societies / RWAs (common facilities, EV charging) | Rs 18,000 per kW | Up to 500 kW, at 3 kW per house |
| Special category states and UTs | Higher benchmark support where notified | Including the North-Eastern states |

**Rs 78,000**Maximum central subsidy per home

**1 crore**Homes targeted

**Rs 75,021 cr**Scheme outlay

**~300 units**Free power a month, the aim

## Who can apply

- An Indian household with its own roof suitable for solar panels
- A valid electricity connection in the household's name
- No earlier central subsidy for rooftop solar on the same connection
- Housing societies and RWAs for common loads, through the society

## How to apply, step by step

- **Register**On the national portal (pmsuryaghar.gov.in) with your state, DISCOM, consumer number and mobile number.
- **Apply**Fill in the rooftop solar application; the DISCOM checks feasibility.
- **Choose a registered vendor**Pick a vendor registered with your DISCOM; agree capacity and price.
- **Install**The vendor installs the system with DCR modules and a compliant inverter.
- **Net meter and inspection**Submit plant details, apply for the net meter; the DISCOM inspects and commissions.
- **Subsidy**After the commissioning certificate is generated on the portal, submit bank details; the subsidy is credited to your account.

Collateral-free loans of around 7% are available from public-sector banks for residential systems up to 3 kW, and the portal links to lenders. Model solar villages in each district receive additional support.

## Getting the most from a home system

- Size to your consumption: a 3 kW system typically generates around 12 units a day in most of India, depending on sunshine and orientation.
- Use a shade-free, south-facing area where you can; avoid water tanks and parapets casting shadows.
- Ask for the DCR module certificate, inverter BIS certificate and warranty documents.
- Keep the panels clean: dust can cut output noticeably in dry months (see [O&M and module cleaning](https://arraysingenieria.com/solar-om-module-cleaning/)).

## Where Arrays Ingenieria fits

PM Surya Ghar is a scheme for homes and housing societies. Arrays Ingenieria focuses on commercial, industrial and tea-estate plants, which fall outside it, and on installation & commissioning for developers. For businesses, the equivalent levers are [accelerated depreciation](https://arraysingenieria.com/accelerated-depreciation-solar/), the [5% GST rate](https://arraysingenieria.com/gst-on-solar-india/) and [net metering](https://arraysingenieria.com/net-metering-india/) or [open access](https://arraysingenieria.com/green-energy-open-access/).

Running a business, school, hospital or housing society with a large roof? We can design a plant that pays back fast.

[Get a free solar quote](https://arraysingenieria.com/free-solar-quote/)

## Frequently asked questions

How much subsidy do I get under PM Surya Ghar?

Rs 30,000 for 1 kW, Rs 60,000 for 2 kW and Rs 78,000 for 3 kW or more. Housing societies get Rs 18,000 per kW for common facilities up to 500 kW.

Can a business get the PM Surya Ghar subsidy?

No. The scheme is for residential households and housing societies. Businesses benefit instead from accelerated depreciation, 5% GST and net metering or open access.

Do I need Indian-made panels?

Yes. Systems under the scheme must use domestically manufactured (DCR) modules and be installed by a vendor registered with your DISCOM.

How long does the subsidy take?

After installation, inspection and net-meter commissioning, the commissioning certificate is generated on the portal and the subsidy is paid to your bank account, typically within weeks.

Guide · Schemes

# PM-KUSUM in 2026: Components A, B and C, New Deadlines and What Comes Next

India's farm solar scheme: up to 2 MW plants on farmers' land, standalone solar pumps and solarised feeders. What each component offers, the 2026 deadline extensions, and the proposed PM-KUSUM 2.0.

On this page

- What PM-KUSUM is
- The three components
- The 2026 deadlines
- What is next: PM-KUSUM 2.0
- Building a Component A or feeder plant: what matters on site
- Frequently asked questions
- Sources

By the [Arrays Ingenieria engineering team](https://arraysingenieria.com/about/) · Updated 11 Oct 2026 · 3 min read

**Key takeaways**

- **Component A:** grid-connected solar plants of 500 kW to 2 MW on farmers' land, with the power bought by the DISCOM
- **Component B:** standalone solar pumps for farms off the grid, with central and state support
- **Component C:** solarising existing grid-connected pumps, individually or by whole agricultural feeders
- 2026: financial closure for Components A and C extended to **30 November 2026**; completion by **31 March 2027**, with no further extension
- A **PM-KUSUM 2.0** with a dedicated agri-PV component has been announced but not yet launched

## What PM-KUSUM is

**Pradhan Mantri Kisan Urja Suraksha evam Utthaan Mahabhiyan (PM-KUSUM)** was launched in March 2019 to give farmers energy security and an extra income from solar, while cutting the diesel and subsidised grid power used for irrigation. It was scaled up and extended in the years since, and in 2026 it is in its final stretch.

## The three components

PM-KUSUM at a glance

| Component | What gets built | Who benefits | Support (typical) |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| A | Grid-connected ground- or stilt-mounted solar plants of 500 kW to 2 MW on barren, fallow or farm land, usually within 5 km of a substation | Farmers, groups, cooperatives, panchayats, FPOs, and developers on their land | DISCOM buys the power at a pre-fixed tariff; DISCOMs receive a performance-based incentive |
| B | Standalone off-grid solar pumps | Individual farmers | Central support of 30% of benchmark cost (50% in the North-East, hill states and islands), plus state support |
| C | Solarisation of existing grid-connected pumps (individual) or of whole agricultural feeders (feeder-level solarisation) | Farmers on grid-connected pumps; DISCOMs for feeders | Central support of 30% (50% in special-category states) for individual pumps; central support for feeder-level plants |

**Why feeder-level solarisation matters**

Instead of panels on every farm, a ground-mount solar plant of a few megawatts feeds an entire agricultural feeder. Farmers get daytime power for irrigation, and the plant is an ordinary utility-style build: land, piling, structures, modules, inverters and a substation connection.

## The 2026 deadlines

PM-KUSUM timelines as revised in 2026

| Milestone | Applies to | Date |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Financial closure | Components A and C | 30 November 2026 (extended from 30 September 2026) |
| Completion (commissioning) | Projects with PPA signed or NTP issued on or before 31 December 2025 | 31 March 2027; no further extension, per MNRE |
| Commissioning, individual pumps | Component B and Component C (individual pump solarisation) | 30 September 2026 under the March 2026 revision; check for later updates |

The extension of financial closure was granted because developers had trouble getting loans appraised and sanctioned in time. MNRE has said there will be no extension of the completion deadline beyond 31 March 2027, so projects that are not under construction by early 2027 are at real risk.

## What is next: PM-KUSUM 2.0

The Union Minister for New and Renewable Energy has said a **PM-KUSUM 2.0** will follow, with a dedicated component of about **10 GW for agri-photovoltaics** (solar panels raised above crops so that farming and generation share the same land). When this guide was checked the new scheme had not been formally notified, so its support levels and eligibility are not yet known.

## Building a Component A or feeder plant: what matters on site

- **Land and soil:** a soil test decides the pile design; farmland often needs deeper piles than hard ground.
- **Evacuation:** the distance to the substation and the line route drive cost and approvals.
- **Security:** chain-link fencing and lighting protect modules on open farmland.
- **Domestic content:** scheme plants must use DCR modules (see [ALMM explained](https://arraysingenieria.com/almm-list-ii-solar-cells/)).
- **Schedule:** with the March 2027 cut-off, piling and structures must start early enough to leave time for commissioning and inspection.

Civil works and chain-link fencing for a 14.36 MW solar project in Uttar Pradesh: the same site works a Component A or feeder-level plant needs.

Developing a PM-KUSUM Component A or feeder-level plant? We do piling, fencing, civil works and installation & commissioning.

[Get a free solar quote](https://arraysingenieria.com/free-solar-quote/)

## Frequently asked questions

What is PM-KUSUM Component A?

Grid-connected solar plants of 500 kW to 2 MW on farmers' land, with the power bought by the DISCOM at a pre-fixed tariff.

What is the last date for PM-KUSUM projects?

Financial closure for Components A and C has been extended to 30 November 2026, and completion is due by 31 March 2027 for projects with PPA or NTP by 31 December 2025, with no further extension.

How much subsidy is there on a solar pump?

Central support is 30% of the benchmark cost (50% in the North-East, hill states and islands), with state support on top; the farmer's share varies by state.

Has PM-KUSUM 2.0 been launched?

It has been announced, with about 10 GW for agri-photovoltaics, but it had not been formally notified when this guide was checked.

Guide · Tea Estates

# Solar for Assam's Tea Estates: Policy, Design and Lessons from Our Plants

Tea estates are among the best solar sites in India: daytime factory load, diesel back-up to cut and land to spare. Assam's policy, how to design for the plucking season, and what we have learnt building plants from Koomber to Harmutty.

On this page

- Why tea estates suit solar so well
- Assam's policy in 2026
- Designing for the plucking season
- The Koomber inauguration
- Lessons from our tea-estate plants
- Frequently asked questions
- Sources

By the [Arrays Ingenieria engineering team](https://arraysingenieria.com/about/) · Updated 11 Oct 2026 · 3 min read

**Key takeaways**

- Assam's Chief Minister has announced that tea garden owners may use up to **5% of their land** for solar generation
- Assam's targets: about **3,500 MW of solar** by 2030 under its solar policy and **6,000 MW of green energy** overall
- Tea factories run hard from about March to November, in daylight, which is exactly when solar generates
- Synchronising solar with the estate's diesel generators cuts diesel use when the grid fails
- The Chief Minister inaugurated our 595 kWp Koomber plant on 1 October 2026; Goodricke has recognised our work at Koomber, Borpatra and Harmutty

## Why tea estates suit solar so well

- **Daytime load.** Withering, rolling, fermenting and drying run through the day in the plucking season.
- **Diesel back-up.** Grid interruptions in rural Assam mean estates run DG sets; every solar unit that replaces diesel saves far more than a grid unit.
- **Land.** Many estates have strips of non-plantation land near the factory, ideal for ground-mount plants.
- **Long horizon.** Estates are run for generations, so a 25-year asset fits naturally.

**5%**Of tea-garden land allowed for solar

**3,500 MW**Assam solar target by 2030

**6,000 MW**Assam green-energy goal, 2030

**595 kWp**Koomber, inaugurated by the CM

## Assam's policy in 2026

In September 2026 the Chief Minister, Dr Himanta Biswa Sarma, wrote that tea garden owners may use up to **5% of their land** for solar generation, as part of the state's goal of **6,000 MW of installed green energy capacity by 2030**. The state's solar promotion policy targets about **3,500 MW of solar by 2030**, with a push for rooftop plants and agri-voltaics, and caps solar on tea-garden land at 5% of the landholding.

Assam's clean-energy policy for industry has also offered tea, coffee and rubber units buying power from APDCL features such as **annual energy banking**, so that surplus solar from the lean months can be drawn in the busy season, with grid-connected rooftop plants capped at 1,000 kW per location under that policy.

**Check the current notification**

Several Assam policies and orders apply, and their names and terms have changed over time. Confirm the current banking, capacity and approval rules with APDCL and the Assam Electricity Regulatory Commission before fixing a design.

## Designing for the plucking season

Design choices for a tea-estate plant

| Question | What we look at | Typical answer |
| --- | --- | --- |
| How big? | Factory load in season, off-season load, sanctioned load, transformer capacity | Sized to daytime factory load in season, within net-metering and transformer limits |
| Rooftop or ground? | Factory roof condition and orientation; available non-plantation land | Ground-mount on spare land is common; it avoids old roofs |
| Diesel? | Number and size of DG sets, how often the grid fails | Synchronise solar with the DG sets so solar runs during outages |
| Export? | Off-season and Sunday surplus | Net metering or banking with APDCL |
| Foundations? | Soil, water table, flooding history | Pile foundations sized to the soil test; raised structures in low-lying land |

At Jay Shree Tea's Towkok and Manjushree estates, the scope included synchronising each plant with two DG sets per site, letting the estates run solar alongside their generators instead of shutting it down when the grid fails.

## The Koomber inauguration

On **1 October 2026** the Chief Minister of Assam inaugurated the **595 kWp** ground-mounted on-grid plant at Koomber Tea Estate in Cachar, part of the 3.11 MW Goodricke Tea Estates Solar Programme with Tata Power Renewable Energy and Sustvest, with Arrays Ingenieria as installation partner.

PB: **Prerana Bharati Digital (PBNN)**Silchar, Assam · on YouTube

### 595 kW solar plant inaugurated at Koomber tea garden

The Arrays Ingenieria team takes the Chief Minister around the Koomber plant after the inauguration.

## Lessons from our tea-estate plants

- **Plan around the season.** Build in the lean months so the plant is ready before plucking peaks.
- **Respect the estate.** Work around labour lines, nurseries and drainage; keep the site clean and safe.
- **Get the approvals moving early.** APDCL feasibility, net metering and inspection take time.
- **Engineer for rain.** Assam's monsoon demands good drainage, raised equipment pads and proper earthing and lightning protection.
- **Hand over properly.** Train the estate electrician, leave drawings and test reports, and set a cleaning routine.

Running a tea estate in Assam or the Dooars? Let us look at your factory load and your land.

[Get a free solar quote](https://arraysingenieria.com/free-solar-quote/)

## Frequently asked questions

Can tea gardens in Assam use their land for solar?

Yes. The Chief Minister has announced that tea garden owners may use up to 5% of their land for solar generation, and the state's solar policy caps solar on tea-garden land at 5% of the landholding.

Can solar work with a tea estate's diesel generators?

Yes. With a DG synchronisation controller the solar plant keeps running during grid outages alongside the generators, cutting diesel use.

Rooftop or ground-mount for a tea factory?

Ground-mount on spare non-plantation land is often better: it avoids old factory roofs and can be sized to the load. Rooftop works where the roof is sound and well oriented.

What size of plant suits a tea estate?

Most estates we work with install between about 200 kWp and 600 kWp, sized to the factory's daytime load in the plucking season and to grid limits.

Guide · Buyer's Guide

# How to Choose a Solar EPC and Installation Partner in India: 12 Questions to Ask

The partner you choose decides how your plant performs for 25 years. Twelve questions to ask any solar EPC or installation contractor, what good answers look like, and the red flags to walk away from.

On this page

- Why the partner matters more than the panel
- The 12 questions
- Red flags
- How to compare quotations fairly
- Our answers
- Frequently asked questions
- Sources

By the [Arrays Ingenieria engineering team](https://arraysingenieria.com/about/) · Updated 11 Oct 2026 · 3 min read

**Key takeaways**

- Ask for **documented** projects: purchase orders, client certificates and site visits, not just photos
- Check who will actually be on site: in-house crews and supervisors, or labour subcontracted at the last minute
- Insist on ALMM-listed modules and BIS-certified inverters named in the contract
- Ask how the contractor handles safety, approvals (DISCOM, CEIG) and testing at handover
- Compare quotations on the same specification; the cheapest bid often hides thinner cables, weaker structures or missing items

## Why the partner matters more than the panel

Two plants built with identical modules can perform very differently. Structure design, cable sizing, earthing, string layout, workmanship at every connector and the quality of commissioning tests decide how much power the plant makes and how safely it runs for 25 years. That is the contractor's work.

## The 12 questions

Questions to ask a solar EPC or installation partner

| # | Question | A good answer looks like |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 1 | Which comparable plants have you built? | Named projects of similar size and type, with locations and dates |
| 2 | Can I see purchase orders, completion or appreciation certificates? | Documents from clients and EPC majors, and references you can call |
| 3 | Who will be on site? | Named project manager and site engineer; in-house crews for critical work |
| 4 | Which modules and inverters, exactly? | Make, model and ALMM / BIS status written into the contract |
| 5 | How is the structure designed? | Wind-load design for your location, galvanising spec, roof or pile calculations |
| 6 | How are cables sized and routed? | Voltage-drop calculation, UV-resistant DC cable, proper trays and glands |
| 7 | How do you earth and protect the plant? | Separate DC and AC earthing, lightning protection, surge devices, tested earth resistance |
| 8 | Who handles approvals? | The contractor files DISCOM, net-metering and CEIG paperwork |
| 9 | What tests will you hand over? | Insulation resistance, polarity, string Voc/Isc, earth resistance, inverter settings, as-built drawings |
| 10 | What is your safety system? | Permits, PPE, work-at-height and electrical isolation procedures, toolbox talks, ISO 45001 |
| 11 | What warranties and guarantees? | Manufacturer warranties passed on, workmanship warranty, performance commitment |
| 12 | What happens after handover? | O&M or module-cleaning options, a contact for faults, response times |

## Red flags

- "Tier-1 equivalent" modules or unnamed inverters in the quotation
- No earthing or lightning-protection design, or a lump sum for "BOS" with no detail
- A price far below others on the same specification
- No site visit before quoting
- Reluctance to put approvals, testing or handover documents in the contract

## How to compare quotations fairly

- **Fix the specification**Capacity (kWp DC and kW AC), module and inverter class, structure type, cable sizes.
- **Ask for a bill of quantities**Line items for modules, inverters, structures, cables, earthing, LA, ACDB/DCDB, civil works, approvals.
- **Compare like with like**Normalise each quote to the same scope; add the missing items to the cheaper ones.
- **Check the generation estimate**The same location and assumptions should give similar yields; an outlier needs explaining.
- **Read the contract**Payment milestones tied to progress, delay and performance clauses, warranty start dates.

## Our answers

Arrays Ingenieria is an ex-servicemen-led company certified to ISO 9001, ISO 14001 and ISO 45001. Our [projects page](https://arraysingenieria.com/projects/) lists our work, and our case studies carry the client certificates and press coverage behind them. We do not manufacture modules or inverters, so we specify and document the makes your project requires.

Our team with the Chief Minister of Assam at the Koomber Tea Estate plant, 1 October 2026.

Put our answers to the test: ask us all 12 questions about your project.

[Get a free solar quote](https://arraysingenieria.com/free-solar-quote/)

## Frequently asked questions

How do I check a solar EPC company's track record?

Ask for named projects of similar size, client purchase orders or certificates, and references you can call. Visit a working plant if you can.

Should the EPC contract name the module and inverter brands?

Yes. The make, model and certification (ALMM for modules, BIS for inverters) should be written into the contract and the bill of quantities.

What documents should I get at handover?

As-built drawings, test reports (insulation, polarity, string voltages and currents, earth resistance), inverter settings, warranty certificates, approvals and an O&M manual.

Is the cheapest solar quote a bad idea?

Not always, but compare quotations on the same specification and bill of quantities. Large price gaps usually come from thinner cables, lighter structures or missing items.

Guide · System Design

# Rooftop vs Ground-Mount Solar: Which Is Right for Your Site?

Use the roof you already have, or build on land? A practical comparison of rooftop and ground-mount solar: cost, space, structure, safety, foundations, approvals and maintenance.

On this page

- The short answer
- Rooftop: what makes a good roof
- Ground-mount: what makes a good site
- When to combine both
- Frequently asked questions
- Sources

By the [Arrays Ingenieria engineering team](https://arraysingenieria.com/about/) · Updated 11 Oct 2026 · 3 min read

**Key takeaways**

- Rooftop uses space you already have and avoids land, fencing and piling costs
- Ground-mount gives freedom to size, orient and maintain the plant, and avoids old or weak roofs
- Industrial sheet roofs need a structural check, purlin-mounted structures and skylight safety mesh
- Ground-mount needs a soil test, pile foundations sized to it, fencing and drainage
- Many sites combine both: rooftop on the sound sheds, ground-mount on spare land

## The short answer

Rooftop and ground-mount solar compared

| Factor | Rooftop | Ground-mount |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Space | Uses existing roofs | Needs land (roughly 4 to 5 acres per MW for fixed-tilt) |
| Cost per kWp | Usually lower: no land, fencing or piling | Higher civil cost, but scale can offset it |
| Size | Limited by roof area and strength | Sized to need (and land available) |
| Orientation and tilt | Follows the roof | Optimised for yield |
| Structure | Purlin clamps or ballast; roof-load check essential | Piles or foundations to the soil test |
| Safety | Work at height; skylight mesh, lifelines, walkways | Ground-level work; fencing and security |
| Maintenance | Access via walkways; roof-wash systems | Easy access; vegetation control |
| Best for | Factories, warehouses, commercial buildings | Tea estates, open-access and captive plants, farms |

## Rooftop: what makes a good roof

- **Strength:** a structural engineer confirms the roof and purlins can carry the added load and wind uplift.
- **Remaining life:** re-roof first if the sheets have only a few years left; removing a plant to re-roof is costly.
- **Shade-free area:** watch for parapets, tanks, chimneys and neighbouring buildings.
- **Safety for life:** skylight safety mesh over translucent sheets, lifelines and walkways for cleaning crews.

A sheet-roof plant at Sitarganj, Uttarakhand. On industrial roofs we install skylight safety mesh so nobody falls through translucent sheets during installation or cleaning.

## Ground-mount: what makes a good site

- **Soil test first:** it decides pile depth and diameter, and whether augered or driven piles suit.
- **Drainage and flooding:** low-lying land needs raised structures and drains.
- **Evacuation:** the distance to your meter or the grid connection point.
- **Security:** chain-link fencing, gates and lighting.
- **Land rules:** in Assam, tea gardens may use up to 5% of their land for solar (see [our tea-estate guide](https://arraysingenieria.com/solar-for-assam-tea-estates-guide/)).

Pile foundations on a utility-scale project. Depth, alignment and levels set the quality of everything built on top.

## When to combine both

Plenty of sites use both: rooftop on sound sheds near the main load, ground-mount on spare land for the rest. The two can feed the same distribution board or separate meters, depending on your connection and state rules.

Not sure which suits your site? Send us a roof photo or a land sketch and your bills.

[Get a free solar quote](https://arraysingenieria.com/free-solar-quote/)

## Frequently asked questions

Is rooftop solar cheaper than ground-mount?

Usually per kWp, because there is no land, fencing or piling. Ground-mount can be competitive at larger scale and gives more freedom in size and orientation.

How much land does a 1 MW ground-mount solar plant need?

Roughly 4 to 5 acres for a fixed-tilt plant, depending on module efficiency, row spacing and the shape of the land.

Can any factory roof take solar panels?

Not always. A structural check of the sheets, purlins and trusses is essential, and old roofs should be replaced before installation.

Why do sheet roofs need skylight mesh?

Translucent skylight sheets cannot take a person's weight. Safety mesh under or over them protects installers and cleaning crews.

Guide · O&M

# Solar O&M and Module Cleaning: Protecting 25 Years of Returns

A solar plant has no moving parts, but it still needs care. Module cleaning, inspections, thermography, inverter and earthing checks, and a practical maintenance schedule that keeps generation where it should be.

On this page

- Why O&M decides your return
- Module cleaning: how, how often and with what
- The maintenance schedule
- Reading the numbers: performance ratio
- Common faults and what causes them
- Frequently asked questions
- Sources

By the [Arrays Ingenieria engineering team](https://arraysingenieria.com/about/) · Updated 11 Oct 2026 · 3 min read

**Key takeaways**

- Dust and bird droppings can cut output noticeably between cleanings, especially in dry, dusty months
- A fixed **module cleaning system** (pipes, valves and nozzles) makes regular washing quick and safe
- Track the **performance ratio** monthly; a falling ratio is the first sign of a problem
- Thermography and string-current checks find hot spots, failed bypass diodes and loose connectors early
- Earthing resistance and lightning protection should be tested every year, before the monsoon

## Why O&M decides your return

A solar plant's return comes from the units it generates over 25 years. Losing even a few per cent of output every year to dirt, tripping inverters or failed strings adds up to years of lost payback. Good operation and maintenance (O&M) protects that output, and keeps the plant safe.

## Module cleaning: how, how often and with what

Cleaning options compared

| Method | How it works | Suits |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Manual with hose and brush | Crews wash with water and soft brushes | Small plants; sites with easy, safe access |
| Fixed module cleaning system (MCS) | A permanent HDPE or uPVC pipe network with valves and hose points across the array | Rooftop and ground plants of any size; fast and safe |
| Robotic cleaning | Waterless or low-water robots run along the rows | Large, uniform utility plants |

Cleaning frequency depends on dust, rain and bird activity: often every one to two weeks in dry, dusty months and less in the monsoon. Use soft or demineralised water where possible, never abrasive tools, and clean in the early morning or late afternoon so cold water does not hit hot glass.

**What we install**

Most of our plants include a module cleaning system: an HDPE or uPVC pipe network from the water tapping point to hose points across the array, so the estate or factory team can wash the modules safely without walking on them.

## The maintenance schedule

A practical O&M schedule

| Frequency | Task |
| --- | --- |
| Daily / remote | Check inverter status and generation on the monitoring portal; investigate alarms |
| Weekly to fortnightly | Module cleaning (more often in dusty months); visual check for damage and shading |
| Monthly | Compare generation with expected; calculate performance ratio; check string currents |
| Quarterly | Inspect DC and AC connections, cable trays, glands and labels; clean inverter filters and vents |
| Half-yearly | Thermographic (infrared) scan of modules and boards; torque check on terminations |
| Yearly, before monsoon | Test earth-pit resistance, lightning arrestors and surge protection; check structure bolts and corrosion |

## Reading the numbers: performance ratio

The **performance ratio (PR)** compares what the plant actually generated with what it should have generated for the sunlight it received. It strips out the weather, so a falling PR points to a plant problem: dirt, a failed string, an inverter derating, or shading from new growth. Track it monthly and act when it drops.

## Common faults and what causes them

- **Hot spots** on modules: cracked cells, failed bypass diodes or persistent shading; found by thermography.
- **Low string current:** a loose MC4 connector, a damaged cable or a dirty or shaded row.
- **Inverter trips:** grid voltage excursions, insulation faults (often moisture in junction boxes) or overheating.
- **Earth faults after rain:** damaged DC cable insulation or water ingress; test insulation resistance.

Want a module cleaning system or an O&M plan for an existing plant? We install and service both.

[Get a free solar quote](https://arraysingenieria.com/free-solar-quote/)

## Frequently asked questions

How often should solar panels be cleaned in India?

Typically every one to two weeks in dry, dusty months and less often in the monsoon. Watch generation: a drop after dry spells shows when cleaning is due.

What is a module cleaning system?

A permanent network of pipes, valves and hose points across a solar array that lets crews wash modules quickly and safely without walking on them.

What is a good performance ratio?

Well-built and well-maintained plants commonly run at about 75% to 85%, depending on climate and design. The trend matters more than the figure.

Do solar plants need maintenance during the monsoon?

Less cleaning, but more electrical attention: check earthing, lightning protection and insulation before and after heavy rain.

Guide · Standards & Safety

# Solar Quality and Safety Norms in India (2026): BIS, the Quality Control Order, CEA and CEIG

What makes a solar plant compliant in 2026: the BIS Quality Control Order for modules, inverters and batteries, the standards each component should meet, the Electrical Inspector's approval, and site safety.

On this page

- Three layers of compliance
- The BIS Quality Control Order
- The standards each component should meet
- CEA safety regulations and CEIG approval
- Safety on site
- Frequently asked questions
- Sources

By the [Arrays Ingenieria engineering team](https://arraysingenieria.com/about/) · Updated 11 Oct 2026 · 3 min read

**Key takeaways**

- The revised **Solar Systems, Devices and Components Goods Order, 2025** (notified 27 January 2025) requires BIS certification for modules, solar inverters and storage batteries
- Large inverters (above 200 kW) were given extra time to certify, reportedly to the end of 2026
- Modules must also meet ALMM where it applies (see our ALMM guide)
- Plants above the voltage and capacity thresholds need the **Electrical Inspector's (CEIG) approval** before energisation under the CEA safety regulations
- Earthing, lightning protection, surge protection and documented commissioning tests are what keep a plant safe for 25 years

## Three layers of compliance

- **Product certification:** each component meets its Indian Standard and carries the BIS mark (and, for modules, ALMM where applicable).
- **Design and installation:** the plant is designed and built to the electrical safety regulations and good practice.
- **Inspection and approval:** the DISCOM and, where required, the Electrical Inspector approve the plant before it is energised.

## The BIS Quality Control Order

MNRE notified the revised **Solar Systems, Devices and Components Goods (Requirement for Compulsory Registration) Order, 2025** in the Gazette on **27 January 2025**, effective after a 180-day transition. It covers **solar PV modules, inverters for solar PV applications and storage batteries**. These must conform to the notified Indian Standards and carry the BIS Standard Mark under a BIS licence; products made only for export are exempt.

Inverters above 200 kW were allowed extra time. MNRE extended the self-certification window for them, reportedly to **31 December 2026**, during which makers need valid IEC certificates matching the Indian Standards.

## The standards each component should meet

Common standards for solar plant components

| Component | Standards to ask for | What they cover |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Crystalline PV modules | IS 14286 / IEC 61215; IS/IEC 61730 | Design qualification and type approval; safety |
| Grid-tied inverters | IS 16221 (Parts 1 and 2) / IEC 62109; IS 16169 | Safety of power converters; islanding-prevention test |
| DC cables | IS 17293 / EN 50618 type solar cables | UV-resistant, double-insulated cables for PV |
| AC power cables | IS 7098 (XLPE) | Armoured LT cables to the distribution board |
| Earthing | IS 3043 | Code of practice for earthing |
| Lightning protection | IS/IEC 62305 | Lightning protection of structures |
| Commissioning and documentation | IEC 62446-1 | System documentation, commissioning tests and inspection |
| Storage batteries | Notified IS for the battery type | Covered by the 2025 Quality Control Order |

**Standards are revised**

BIS revises standards and adds parts over time, and sources differ on which part covers what. Ask the supplier for the BIS licence and test reports for the exact model supplied, and keep them in the project file.

## CEA safety regulations and CEIG approval

The Central Electricity Authority's **safety and electric supply regulations** set the rules for electrical installations, including clearances, earthing, protection and inspection. Installations above the specified voltage, and in many states above a set capacity, must be inspected and approved by the **Electrical Inspector** (the Chief Electrical Inspector to Government, CEIG, in many states) before they are energised.

- **Drawing approval**Submit single-line diagram, layout and equipment details for approval where the state requires it.
- **Build to the approved design**Install with the specified protection, earthing and clearances.
- **Test**Insulation resistance, earth resistance, protection settings and relay tests, recorded on the prescribed formats.
- **Inspection**The Electrical Inspector inspects the installation and the test records.
- **Approval to energise**With approval, the DISCOM completes metering and synchronisation.

**Our practice**

We handle CEIG approvals and liaison as part of our scope on many projects, from rooftop plants on industrial sheds to ground-mount plants, and keep the test records the inspector expects.

## Safety on site

- Permit-to-work and electrical isolation (lock-out, tag-out) before any work on live DC or AC circuits
- Work-at-height controls on roofs: lifelines, harnesses, edge protection and skylight safety mesh
- PPE suited to the task: helmets, insulated gloves, safety shoes, eye protection
- Daily toolbox talks and supervision by trained engineers
- A safety management system certified to ISO 45001

Earthing and electrical safety works on a solar plant: a 25-year plant is only as safe as its earthing and protection.

Need a plant that passes inspection first time? Our veteran-led crews build to the standards and document every test.

[Get a free solar quote](https://arraysingenieria.com/free-solar-quote/)

## Frequently asked questions

Do solar inverters need BIS certification?

Yes. Under the 2025 Quality Control Order, inverters for solar PV applications must carry the BIS Standard Mark. Inverters above 200 kW were given extra time, reportedly to the end of 2026.

Which standards should solar modules meet?

IS 14286 / IEC 61215 for design qualification and IS/IEC 61730 for safety, and ALMM listing where the project falls under the ALMM order.

What is CEIG approval for solar?

Approval by the Electrical Inspector that the installation meets the CEA safety regulations, required before energising plants above the specified voltage or, in many states, above a set capacity.

What tests should be done at commissioning?

Insulation resistance, polarity, string open-circuit voltage and short-circuit current, earth resistance, protection settings and functional checks, documented to IEC 62446-1.

Guide · Storage

# Battery Storage with Solar in India (2026): Mandates, Incentives and When It Pays

Storage is becoming part of India's solar story. The two-hour co-located storage advisory for tenders, the viability gap funding for batteries, transmission waivers, the draft rule for large prosumers, and when a battery makes sense for a business.

On this page

- Why storage is arriving now
- The policy picture
- When a battery pays for a business
- Designing solar-plus-storage
- Frequently asked questions
- Sources

By the [Arrays Ingenieria engineering team](https://arraysingenieria.com/about/) · Updated 11 Oct 2026 · 3 min read

**Key takeaways**

- A February 2025 Power Ministry advisory asks for **two-hour co-located storage equal to 10% of solar capacity** in future solar tenders
- Viability gap funding (VGF) supports battery storage; a second tranche of about **Rs 5,400 crore** was announced in 2025
- Co-located battery projects commissioned by **30 June 2028** keep an ISTS charges waiver under the 2025 amendment
- The **draft 2026 consumer-rules amendment** proposes storage for renewable installations above 500 kW
- For C&I owners, storage pays where evening tariffs are high, diesel back-up is costly or export is restricted

## Why storage is arriving now

Solar generates in the middle of the day; demand peaks in the evening. As solar grows past 170 GW, grids need to move cheap daytime energy into the evening. Battery prices have fallen sharply, so policy is now nudging storage into new solar projects.

## The policy picture

Storage policy in India, 2025-2026

| Measure | What it does | Status |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Co-located storage in solar tenders | Two-hour storage equal to 10% of the solar capacity in future tenders by implementing agencies and states | Ministry of Power advisory, February 2025; applies to future tenders, not existing projects or PM Surya Ghar |
| Viability gap funding for BESS | Central support to make grid batteries viable | Second tranche of about Rs 5,400 crore announced in 2025 |
| ISTS charges waiver | Waiver for co-located BESS commissioned by 30 June 2028 (where power is consumed outside the host state), and for pumped storage awarded by that date | Amended in June 2025 |
| Storage for large prosumers | Renewable installations above 500 kW may need storage | Proposed in the March 2026 draft consumer-rules amendment |

**Advisory, draft and final**

Some of these are advisories or drafts. Tender documents and final notifications decide what is binding for a given project.

## When a battery pays for a business

- **Evening peak tariffs:** with time-of-day tariffs, shifting solar into the peak is worth more (see [net metering and ToD](https://arraysingenieria.com/net-metering-india/)).
- **Diesel back-up:** estates and factories that run DG sets during outages can cut diesel use.
- **Export limits:** where exports are capped or poorly paid, storing surplus beats spilling it.
- **Demand charges:** trimming peaks can lower contract demand.

Where none of these apply, a solar plant sized to daytime load, without storage, usually gives the fastest payback.

## Designing solar-plus-storage

- Decide the job: peak shifting, back-up, or both. That sets kW and kWh.
- Choose the coupling: AC-coupled batteries are simpler to add to an existing plant; DC-coupled suit new builds.
- Specify certified batteries and a battery management system; storage batteries fall under the BIS Quality Control Order.
- Plan fire safety, ventilation and space, and get the approvals the DISCOM and Electrical Inspector require.

Thinking about adding storage to an existing plant? We can review your load and tariff first.

[Get a free solar quote](https://arraysingenieria.com/free-solar-quote/)

## Frequently asked questions

Is battery storage mandatory with solar in India?

Not for most existing or private projects. A February 2025 advisory asks for two-hour storage equal to 10% of capacity in future solar tenders, and a 2026 draft proposes storage for installations above 500 kW.

What is VGF for battery storage?

Viability gap funding: central support that covers part of the cost of grid battery projects to make them viable. A second tranche of about Rs 5,400 crore was announced in 2025.

Does a factory need a battery with rooftop solar?

Usually not. A plant sized to daytime load gives the fastest payback. Storage pays where evening tariffs are high, diesel back-up is costly or exports are restricted.

## Sources

- [Mercom India: Government mandates two-hour energy storage in solar tenders](https://www.mercomindia.com/government-mandates-two-hour-energy-storage-integration-in-solar-tenders)

Guide · Installation & Commissioning

# Solar Plant Installation and Commissioning: The Complete Step-by-Step Checklist

What actually happens between the purchase order and the day a solar plant goes live. Every stage of installation and commissioning, the tests that prove the plant is safe, and the documents you should receive at handover.

On this page

- Before anyone picks up a tool
- Stage by stage: installation
- Commissioning: the tests that prove the plant
- Inspection, approvals and going live
- What you should receive at handover
- Frequently asked questions
- Sources

By the [Arrays Ingenieria engineering team](https://arraysingenieria.com/about/) · Updated 11 Oct 2026 · 3 min read

**Key takeaways**

- Installation runs in a fixed order: civil works, structures, modules, DC cabling, inverters, AC side, earthing and protection
- Every connection is a potential fault: torque, crimping, gland sealing and labelling matter
- Commissioning proves the plant: insulation resistance, polarity, string voltages and currents, earth resistance, protection and grid tests
- Inspection and approvals (DISCOM, CEIG) come before energisation
- At handover you should receive as-built drawings, test reports, warranties, approvals and an O&M manual

## Before anyone picks up a tool

- Approved layout and single-line diagram; structure and foundation design
- Safety plan, permits and inductions for every worker; the client's site rules signed off
- Material receipt checks: module and inverter models, serial numbers and certificates matched to the specification
- A storage area that keeps modules flat, dry and secure

## Stage by stage: installation

- **Civil works**Earth-pit chambers and covers, equipment foundations for inverters, ACDB and ITB, cable trenches, and for ground-mount plants the piles or foundations, drainage and fencing.
- **Module mounting structures**Erect and align the structures to the design tilt and levels; torque every bolt; on sheet roofs, fix to purlins with the right clamps and seal every penetration.
- **Module installation**Mount modules with the specified clamps and torque; keep gaps for expansion; do not stand on modules.
- **DC cabling and stringing**Connect module to module and run string cables in UV-protected conduit or trays to the combiner boxes or inverters; crimp MC4 connectors with the right tool; label every string.
- **Inverters**Mount inverters on their stands or foundations with ventilation clearance; terminate DC and AC cables; configure grid settings.
- **AC side**Lay armoured AC cables to the ACDB and the point of connection; terminate with proper glands and lugs.
- **Earthing and protection**Separate DC and AC earthing with tested earth pits; lightning arrestors; surge protection devices; equipotential bonding of structures.
- **Ancillaries**Module cleaning system, walkways or lifelines, safety signage, fire extinguishers and monitoring.

The AC distribution board and inauguration banner at the 230 kWp Borpatra Tea Estate plant, Assam: the point where the solar plant meets the estate's supply.

## Commissioning: the tests that prove the plant

Commissioning tests and what they show

| Test | What it checks | Typical acceptance |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Visual inspection | Damage, mounting, cable routing, labels, clearances | No defects; matches drawings |
| Polarity and continuity | Every string wired correctly | Correct polarity on every string |
| String open-circuit voltage (Voc) | Correct number of modules and no faulty ones | Within a few per cent of expected for the conditions |
| String short-circuit or operating current | Strings performing alike | Strings matched within tolerance for the irradiance |
| Insulation resistance | No leakage from DC conductors to earth | Above the minimum for the system voltage |
| Earth resistance | Earthing system effective | Within the design value |
| Inverter functional tests | Start-up, grid synchronisation, anti-islanding and protection settings | Operates and trips as specified |
| Performance check | Output against irradiance | Consistent with the design yield |

Tests are recorded on formats that follow IEC 62446-1 and the DISCOM's and Electrical Inspector's requirements, so the same records serve the client, the approvals and future O&M.

## Inspection, approvals and going live

- DISCOM inspection and, where required, the Electrical Inspector's (CEIG) inspection
- Installation of the bidirectional or generation meter
- Synchronisation with the grid and, at tea estates and factories with diesel back-up, with the DG sets
- Commissioning certificate and, for scheme projects, portal updates

## What you should receive at handover

- As-built layout and single-line diagram
- Test reports for every string and every test above
- Equipment list with serial numbers, warranty certificates and BIS / ALMM documents
- Approvals: DISCOM, net-metering or open-access, CEIG
- O&M manual, cleaning procedure and a contact for faults
- Training for the site electrician or estate team

On many of our projects the installation & commissioning scope also includes collecting the warranty certificates and the client's I&C-cum-handover certificate, so the plant owner and the EPC both close the project with a complete file.

Need an installation & commissioning partner for a rooftop or ground-mount plant? Our veteran-led crews work Pan-India.

[Get a free solar quote](https://arraysingenieria.com/free-solar-quote/)

## Frequently asked questions

What does installation and commissioning (I&C) of a solar plant include?

Civil works for equipment, mounting structures, module installation, DC and AC cabling, inverters, earthing and protection, then testing, inspection, grid synchronisation and handover.

How long does it take to install a 1 MW solar plant?

With materials on site and approvals moving, installation of a 1 MW rooftop or ground-mount plant typically takes several weeks; approvals can add more. Weather and site access matter.

What tests are done when a solar plant is commissioned?

Visual inspection, polarity and continuity, string Voc and current, insulation resistance, earth resistance, inverter functional and protection tests, and a performance check.

What documents should I get after solar installation?

As-built drawings, test reports, equipment and warranty documents, approvals, an O&M manual and training for your team.
